previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, pulmonary hypertension, and chronic vertigo was admitted after missing two dialysis sessions due to severe vertigo and vomiting. She presented with hyperkalemia (potassium 6.7) at an outside hospital, received emergency treatment, and was transferred for further management. She underwent two consecutive hemodialysis sessions, which normalized her potassium and improved her symptoms. Meclizine was continued for vertigo, and physical therapy recommended outpatient vestibular rehabilitation. The patient refused telemetry due to adhesive allergy but was closely monitored. She remained stable, was discharged home in good condition, and advised to monitor weight, attend dialysis regularly, and follow up with her primary care provider.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
It is normal to have slight swelling of the legs:
 Elevate your leg above the level of your heart with pillows 
every ___ hours throughout the day and night
 Avoid prolonged periods of standing or sitting without your 
legs elevated
 It is normal to feel tired and have a decreased appetite, your 
appetite will return with time 
 Drink plenty of fluids and eat small frequent meals
 It is important to eat nutritious food options (high fiber, 
lean meats, vegetables/fruits, low fat, low cholesterol) to 
maintain your strength and assist in wound healing
 To avoid constipation: eat a high fiber diet and use stool 
softener while taking pain medication

ACTIVITIES:
 When you go home, you may walk and use stairs
 You may shower (let the soapy water run over groin incision, 
rinse and pat dry)
 Your incision may be left uncovered, unless you have small 
amounts of drainage from the wound, then place a dry dressing or 
band aid over the area 
 No heavy lifting, pushing or pulling (greater than 5 lbs) for 
1 week (to allow groin puncture to heal)
 After 1 week, you may resume sexual activity
 After 1 week, gradually increase your activities and distance 
walked as you can tolerate

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  RENAL TRANSPLANT U.S. RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with new finding on CT of right transplant
kidney with ? aneurism. New pain in RLQ with weight loss. See CT scan.  // R/o
aneurism/infection right transplant kidney.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale as well as color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images
of the renal transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen dated ___.
Arterial ultrasound dated ___.
CT abdomen dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

The native kidneys are atrophic bilaterally.  No evidence of hydronephrosis. 
No masses are visualized.

Within the right lower quadrant, in the transplant bed, at the area of concern
there is a 3.9 x 3.1 x 2.4 cm oblong, lobulated, pulsatile structure with
arterial feeding flow with a ___ appearance consistent with a
pseudoaneurysm.  The pseudoaneurysm arises from the transplanted vessel off
the right external iliac artery and the neck measures 0.5 cm.  This
pseudoaneurysm corresponds with the round hyperdense structure within the
right lower quadrant seen on the CT dated ___.  The pseudoaneurysm
appears to have increased in size since the CT dated ___.

Limited views of the aorta are normal.

IMPRESSION: 

3.9 cm pseudoaneurysm within the right lower quadrant arising from the right
external iliac artery with a neck measuring 0.5 cm, corresponding to the
hyperdense structure on the recent CT, which has increased in size since ___.  The patient reports increasing pain in this region and
therefore after discussion with the ordering clinician was sent to the
emergency room for further assessment

NOTIFICATION:  The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by
___, M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 9:41 AM, 5 minutes after
discovery of the findings.

The patient was subsequently referred to the emergency department.

EXAMINATION:  CTA AORTA/BIFEM/ILIAC RUNOFF W/WANDWO C AND RECONS

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with R iliac aneurysm, progressing in size and
painful.  Assess for active aneurysm disruption.

TECHNIQUE:  Abdomen and pelvis CTA: Non-contrast and multiphasic post-contrast
images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis.
Oral contrast was not administered.
MIP reconstructions were performed on independent workstation and reviewed on
PACS.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 1,085 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT pelvis ___, ___.

FINDINGS: 

VASCULAR:

There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is moderate calcium burden in
the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.  Left renal artery is small.
Dense atherosclerotic calcifications seen at the origin of the right renal
artery which does not opacify distally.

LOWER CHEST: Mild, right greater than left, bibasilar atelectasis is noted in
the lung bases. There is no pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The visualized liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation
throughout. There is no evidence of focal lesions based on arterial phase.
There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The
gallbladder is is resected.

PANCREAS: Within the pancreatic head, body, and tail are multiple scattered
0.4 cm hypodensities (3A: 31, 37, 40) as well as 0.7 cm (3A:  42, 35)
hypodensities better seen on today's exam.  The pancreas otherwise has normal
attenuation throughout, without pancreatic ductal dilatation. There is no
peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: Bilateral native kidneys are atrophic with scattered bilateral
subcentimeter cysts largest measuring 1 cm (03:46) within the left upper pole
and 0.8 cm in the right lower pole, unchanged since prior examination.  The
transplanted kidney within the right iliac fossa has been surgically removed.

GASTROINTESTINAL:  Small hiatal hernia.  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal
caliber, wall thickness and enhancement throughout. Colon and rectum are
within normal limits.  Appendix is not visualized however no secondary signs
of acute appendicitis.

RETROPERITONEUM:  Numerous scattered subcentimeter retroperitoneal and
mesenteric lymph nodes do not meet CT size criteria for enlargement are stable
since prior examination.

PELVIS: Right pelvic sidewall heterogeneous lesion with internal low-density
components and calcifications is most compatible with chronic hematoma in the
region of the postoperative bed of prior, since removed right pelvic renal
transplant.  This heterogeneous area measures approximately 4.1 x 5.1 cm
unchanged since ___.  Along the posterior aspect of this chronic
hematoma is a 4 x 3 cm (3:100) (previously 3.7 x 2.9 cm) enhancing lesion in
direct continuity with the external iliac artery which matches blood pool on
the delayed phase consistent with a pseudoaneurysm.  This has slightly
increased in size.  The right external iliac artery adjacent to this hematoma
slightly irregular in appearance, unchanged since prior examination and likely
related to prior renal transplant anastomosis.  There several adjacent lymph
nodes in the retroperitoneum, 1 abutting the distal external iliac artery (3B:
388)

The bladder is decompressed.  Multiple top-normal bilateral pelvic sidewall
lymph nodes are stable since prior examination, largest measuring 1 cm in
short axis (3:127) along the right pelvic sidewall. There is no free fluid in
the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus and ovaries are not visualized.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES:  Small fat containing umbilical hernia.  Abdominal and pelvic
wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. Minimal increase in size of pseudoaneurysm arising the right external iliac
artery now measuring 4 cm adjacent to a chronic right pelvic sidewall hematoma
in the postoperative bed of previously removed renal transplant.

2. Multiple pancreatic head and body hypodensities, are statistically likely
to represent side branch IPMNs.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Follow-up MRI abdomen as previously recommended.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal view of the chest

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

Elevation of right hemidiaphragm is similar to before.  Mild bibasilar

IMPRESSION: 

No acute cardiopulmonary process.
